source_read: PDF (version of record, J Clin Exp Neuropsychol 27:189–204, Taylor & Francis download with an unnumbered cover page): all 17 PDF pages read (printed pp. 189–204 = PDF pp. 2–17); Table 1, all four pages of Table 2 and the numbers in the running text on pp. 193–194 and 200 checked on pages rendered at 150 dpi; Table 2 transcribed and recounted (140 rows) and its median recomputed.

claims.overstatement: The statement does not overstate this source; it rightly drops the review's causal wording (aim stated as deficits 'found as a result of cocaine use', p. 191; 'cocaine use had the largest effect', p. 194). Two problems sit in the magnitude: (1) it says 'Positive values mean poorer performance in the cocaine group unless stated' but then lists WAIS-R Digit Symbol −0.49, Rey-Osterrieth delayed recall −0.45 and WAIS-R Arithmetic −0.66 with the printed signs; in this paper the sign follows each test's scoring, and these three negative values are lower scores in the cocaine groups, which the review treats as deficits (pp. 193–194). Under the claim's convention they read as better performance; they should be written as 0.49, 0.45 and 0.66 or flagged as 'lower scores'. The sign of Stroop colour-word interference −0.11 cannot be interpreted from the paper (no sign convention is stated, Table 2 note p. 198), so it should be given as about 0.1 with direction unclear rather than as a value favouring the cocaine group. (2) '93 from one study' (magnitude) and '93 of them from a single study' (statement) read as if one study supplied 93 measures; the 93 rows each rest on one study, from several different studies (for example the WAIS rows from a sample of 61 vs 63, the MicroCog rows from 20 vs 29, the BMAE rows from 20 vs 20). Suggest 'each resting on a single study'.
claims.note: Everything in the statement that comes from this source checks: 15 studies, 481 vs 586, eligibility window 1987–2002, median 0.35, 140 rows with 93 single-study rows (my recount), Trail Making B 0.49 (9), Trail Making A 0.19 (10), Stroop colour-word interference −0.11 (7), largest values about 1 from single small studies with the largest (Speech Sounds Perception 1.09) favouring the cocaine group, abstinence 0 to 1075.5 days (about 2.9 years). Recomputed median of the absolute Table 2 values is 0.335 (0.355 if the six zero rows are left out), signed median −0.265, so the printed 0.35 is of absolute values. Editors' calculation supporting 'smaller' for multi-study measures: median absolute value 0.41 for the 93 single-study rows against 0.23 for the 47 multi-study rows; Trail Making B (0.49) is itself above the overall median. Minor points: the 15 included studies (asterisked in the references) were published 1992–2002, so 1987–2002 is the eligibility window, not the span of the studies; the 586 controls conflict with Table 1's mean control-sample size of 36 (15 × 36 = 540). Checks the brief asks for: abstinence reported by 11 of 15 studies (median 23.6 days, range 0–1075.5) and not analysed; comparison groups were 'matched normal healthy controls' but no control age, education or other drug use is reported, so the claim's 'comparison groups often had more education and were younger' gets no support (and no contradiction) from this source; alcohol abuse (not dependence) was allowed and several samples included concurrent caffeine, nicotine and alcohol use, with no adjustment; no comparison with test norms is made, so the review cannot say whether the cocaine groups' scores were within the normal range (the only norm reference is the primary authors' remark that controls scored low on Speech Sounds Perception). The review covers memory and attention, not inhibition of a started response or decision making (one go/no-go row, −0.19).

anchors.locator: Abstract (p. 189); Method › Criteria for Inclusion, 1st paragraph (p. 192); Results, 1st paragraph (p. 193)
anchors.extracted: 15 studies met the criteria: published 1987–2002, statistics convertible to d, DSM-III-R or DSM-IV cocaine abuse or dependence, matched healthy control group; concurrent alcohol abuse (not dependence) allowed. Test results from 481 people in the cocaine groups and 586 healthy controls; only the first testing occasion used. Included studies (asterisks, pp. 202–204) date 1992–2002 (one undated).

Median effect size across all tests 0.35. Table 2 has 140 test-variable rows, 93 with a single effect size and 47 with two to ten (my count). Recomputed: median absolute d 0.335 (0.355 excluding six rows at 0.00); single-study rows median 0.41, multi-study rows 0.23 (editors' calculation).

anchors.locator: Table 2: WAIS-R Arithmetic (p. 195); Trail Making Test Part B, WAIS-R Digit Symbol, ROCF Delay (p. 196); Trail Making Test Part A, Stroop Color-Word Interference Test (p. 197)
anchors.extracted: Mean d (number of ds; SD; cocaine vs control n): Trail Making B 0.49 (9; 0.25; 300 vs 344); Trail Making A 0.19 (10; 0.51; 330 vs 374); Stroop Color-Word Interference −0.11 (7; 0.67; 243 vs 308); WAIS-R Digit Symbol −0.49 (6; 0.46; 170 vs 145); ROCF delayed recall −0.45 (6; 0.35; 205 vs 244); WAIS-R Arithmetic −0.66 (5; 0.48; 146 vs 100). Unweighted means of study ds (Method, p. 191), no confidence intervals; sign convention not stated (Table 2 note, p. 198).

Four largest rows, all single studies: Speech Sounds Perception 1.09 (30 vs 30), on which the cocaine group performed better, attributed by the primary authors to chance and to controls scoring low against external norms; grooved pegboard −1.07 (20 vs 29); BMAE oral fluency 1.04 (20 vs 20, direction not discussed); MicroCog executive function −1.00 (20 vs 29).

Length of abstinence reported by 11 studies: median 23.6 days, mean 128.7 (SD 317.0), range 0–1075.5 days. The authors raise acute intoxication versus abstinence; no moderator analysis was possible with the data (age, education, duration or amount of use not analysed).

anchors.locator: Method › Criteria for Inclusion (p. 192); Discussion, 12th paragraph (p. 201)
anchors.extracted: Alcohol dependence excluded but alcohol abuse allowed; several samples included concurrent caffeine, nicotine and alcohol use; the authors say the differences could be at least partly due to alcohol and did not analyse it. No control-group age, education or drug use reported (Table 1 describes cocaine groups only).

key_findings.correction: Numbers and locators confirmed (median 0.35; U2 mean 0.58, median 0.57, range 0.50–0.70; 140 rows, 93 single-study; my recomputation also gives 0.335 and 0.573, signed median −0.265). Wording suggestion: '93 of them each from a single study', because the claim built on this card now says '93 from one study', which misreads it.

All eight rows, n's and page locators confirmed. Note for the editor: the card's note (all eight point to poorer performance under usual scoring) is right, but the claim's magnitude lists three of them with negative signs under a 'positive = poorer' convention.

reporting_issues.note: Found independently: 15 × 36 = 540 against 586; the cocaine side (15 × 32 = 480 against 481) agrees.
Recomputed: the 8-effect COWAT row plus BMAE oral fluency (1.04) gives mean −0.0533 and SD 0.519 (n−1), and 265+20 = 285, 336+20 = 356, exactly the 9-effect row.
Rows checked in Table 2 (BMAE oral fluency 1.04, Hooper 0.40, RAVLT total 0.37, WAIS-R Verbal IQ 0.36, RAVLT delayed 0.35); p. 190 notes better verbal fluency in some primary studies.

Values confirmed. Strictly, the abstract says moderate to large effects were 'obtained on tests of' visual and working memory, and some such rows do exceed 0.50 (BVRT number correct −0.71, RMT picture recall −0.69, PASAT −0.66), so 'selective' (the consequence) is the right word rather than 'contradicted'.
Recounted: 14 attention measures named above the median on pp. 193–194, 9 of them single-study; the five multi-study ones range 0.49 to 0.68 in absolute value.
Found independently (p. 194 'third largest' vs second in Table 2, p. 195); finger tapping, right −0.61 (30 vs 21) confirmed.
Robinson et al. 1999 (p. 203) and Di Sclafani et al. 2002 (p. 202) are asterisked; their titles name alcohol-dependent groups.
The Goldstein et al. entry on p. 202 has no year. The cross-check against López-Martín's list is checked in my López-Martín output.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 critically low: no protocol, two databases with an unjustified English-only limit, no excluded-study list, no appraisal of included studies, unweighted means without intervals or heterogeneity statistics (Method, p. 191), no publication-bias assessment. I agree with every domain judgment.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: causal aim and conclusions, an abstract attention range whose upper end is a result favouring the cocaine group, and an abstract domain summary that does not match Table 2.

missed: The 15 included studies (asterisked, pp. 202–204) were published 1992–2002 (Goldstein et al. undated); the card's 'published 1987–2002' (design_detail, can_establish) describes the eligibility window, not the studies.
The printed median of 0.35 is reproduced exactly only if the six rows at 0.00 are left out (0.355); over all 140 rows it is 0.335. Trivial, but it explains the card's 'about 0.34'.
Editors' calculation that supports the claim's 'smaller on multi-study measures': median absolute d 0.41 for the 93 single-study rows against 0.23 for the 47 multi-study rows.

The review never compares the cocaine groups' scores with test norms (apart from the Speech Sounds remark), so it cannot say whether any group difference lies within the normal range; the card says so under validity_norms but no key finding records it, and the claim's memory-and-thinking checks need it.
